title: Keep Body Comments Off the Menu | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children

narration.transcript: At a family meal, someone comments on a child's body or on how much is on their plate. You can redirect the conversation. Pause before laughing along. Even casual remarks can make bodies and eating feel like something everyone is entitled to judge. Try: Let us leave body comments out of dinner. I would love to hear about what you have been enjoying lately. Notice your own talk too. You can discuss people, interests and everyday experiences without rating your body or somebody else's food. This is a communication boundary, not a nutrition treatment. If you are worried about your child's eating or health, speak privately with a qualified professional.
